blocked.name: Quercus sinuata var. breviloba, Texas Big Tree Registry TreeID 970
sources: Texas Big Tree Registry, Texas A&M Forest Service (texasforestinfo.tamu.edu/BigTreeRegistry). Non-commercial licence: usable as a lead and verification source, never imported. See OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md.
blocked.why_blocked: PRIVATE LAND. The Texas Big Tree Registry's PublicOrPrivate flag is 0 on this tree, and the flag is not the undocumented mystery an earlier pass took it for: across all 660 swept trees, flag 1 belongs to Big Bend and Guadalupe Mountains National Parks, Sam Houston National Forest, state natural areas and TxDOT districts, while flag 0 belongs to Big Tree Ranch, X-Arrow Ranch, Little Sandy Hunting & Fishing Club and similar. It means what it says. The registry also sets Display 0 on almost all of them, so it withholds these locations from its own public map, and hard rule 10 is absolute about not undoing that: the coordinates only reached us because the backend returns what the front end hides. Never ship unless a source shows the site is genuinely open to visitors.

notes.note: Swept from the corrected Texas Big Tree Registry pull (scripts/texas_big_trees.py). Circumference is INCHES: an earlier Houston pass read it as centimetres and concluded the state was thin. Coordinates decide which city a tree belongs to, never CountyName.

PublicOrPrivate decoded from the data itself: flag 1 is national parks, national forests, state natural areas and TxDOT; flag 0 is ranches and hunting clubs. Flag 0 trees moved to blocked under hard rule 10, since the registry also hides them from its own public map and their coordinates only reached us because the backend returns what the front end withholds. OrganizationName names the owner and is the field a verify pass should lead with.
